name: history
summary: Shows the history of typed commands.
description: Shell builtin that lists previous commands, numbered. The history is saved to ~/.bash_history when the shell closes. Useful shortcuts: !42 reruns command no. 42, !! reruns the last one (sudo !! to rerun it with sudo), and Ctrl+R searches the history as you type.

options.description: Clears the history of the current session.
Deletes the entry at this position.
Writes the session history to ~/.bash_history right away.
Appends the session’s new commands to the history file.

arguments.name: N
arguments.description: Shows only the last N commands.

examples.output:
498  cd project
  499  git status
  500  npm test
  501  git commit -m "fix"
  502  history 5

examples.explanation: Finds SSH connections you have already typed.
Deletes entry 501, for example if it contained a password.
